modules.title: Copilot Studio agent design and management
modules.summary: Build, ground, publish, monitor, and govern Copilot Studio agents with topics, knowledge sources, tools, channels, analytics, and evaluations.

lessons.title: Build agents with topics, knowledge, and tools
lessons.summary: Understand the core pieces of a Copilot Studio agent: purpose, instructions, topics, trigger phrases, knowledge sources, generative answers, tools, agent flows, connectors, and MCP servers.
learningObjectives: Identify topics, trigger phrases, instructions, and knowledge sources in an agent
Describe how tools, agent flows, connectors, and MCP servers extend agents
Explain when generative answers use grounded knowledge
Choose building blocks for a simple Copilot Studio agent scenario
lessons.explanation:
A useful agent is a well-designed teammate with a job description, approved information, and safe ways to act. **Microsoft Copilot Studio** is a low-code studio for building and managing agents and workflows. In the HR Helper lab, Contoso creates an agent that answers HR policy questions, uses internal SharePoint knowledge, asks follow-up questions, and publishes to employee channels.

Start with the use case. Agents are good for repeatable conversations: employee help, customer support, IT triage, policy Q&A, guided service requests, and task automation. Then define instructions: what the agent should help with, tone, boundaries, and escalation rules.

A **topic** defines how a conversation progresses. Trigger phrases such as 'request time off' or 'how many vacation days' help the agent recognize a path. **Knowledge sources** ground answers in enterprise information such as websites, SharePoint, Dataverse, or other approved systems.

**Tools** let an agent do work. A tool can use a connector, an agent flow, or a Model Context Protocol server to interact with external systems. For PL-900, focus on the concept: knowledge helps answer; topics guide conversation; tools act.

terminology.definition: A low-code studio for building and managing agents and workflows.
An AI-powered experience that can converse, use knowledge, and perform actions.
Example wording that can start a topic.
Approved data used to ground answers.
A callable capability that performs an action.

lessons.businessScenario: Contoso HR needs HR Helper to answer policy questions from SharePoint and guide time-off requests.
lessons.technicalExample: Agent design: instructions, SharePoint knowledge, Request time off topic, question node, condition, message, and optional case-creation tool.

misconception.myth: A Copilot Studio agent only needs one large prompt to be useful.
misconception.reality: Useful agents combine scoped instructions, topics for predictable paths, knowledge sources for grounded answers, and tools or agent flows for actions.

lessons.examTakeaway: When the scenario says answer from policy, think knowledge source; when it says guide a user through steps, think topic; when it says create, update, send, or retrieve, think tool or agent flow.
lessons.recap: Understand the core pieces of a Copilot Studio agent: purpose, instructions, topics, trigger phrases, knowledge sources, generative answers, tools, agent flows, connectors, and MCP servers.
lessons.simplerExplanation: Building an agent is like staffing a reception desk: the receptionist needs a job description, a handbook, a call script, and approved forms—not just a friendly personality.
lessons.anotherExample: Wide World Importers creates a supplier FAQ agent with a SharePoint knowledge source for policy answers, a topic for onboarding questions, and a connector tool to open a vendor-support case.

lessons.title: Design grounded and helpful agent conversations
lessons.summary: Create better agent conversations by combining clear instructions, realistic trigger phrases, focused questions, grounded answers, confirmations, tools, and escalation paths.
learningObjectives: Write clear agent instructions for a focused business purpose
Identify trigger phrases and questions that guide useful conversations
Explain why grounded answers, confirmations, and escalation improve reliability
Choose a conversation design that avoids unsupported or unsafe answers
lessons.explanation:
The fun part of an agent is the conversation; the hard part is making it reliable. A good Copilot Studio agent should feel like a calm coworker: it understands the request, asks only what it needs, uses approved knowledge, confirms actions, and knows when to hand off.

Start with intent. Trigger phrases should sound like real users: 'request time off,' 'book vacation,' or 'how do I take sick leave?' In the topic, keep the path short. Ask one question at a time, store answers in variables, and branch when the next step depends on the answer.

Use knowledge sources for broad policy and FAQ answers. Generative answers can summarize relevant information, but they should be grounded in approved content. Keep instructions specific: answer HR policy questions, cite approved sources when used, and escalate personal disputes or confidential issues.

Tools make conversations powerful but also risky. A connector action, agent flow, or MCP tool can create records, send emails, or query systems. Add confirmation before submitting data, especially when a tool changes records or sends messages.

terminology.definition: The sequence of nodes and decisions an agent follows.
An AI-generated response grounded in configured knowledge.
A stored value from the conversation.
A planned handoff to a person or support path.
A deterministic workflow an agent can invoke.
A server that exposes resources and tools through Model Context Protocol.

lessons.businessScenario: Northwind Traders wants an employee agent that explains travel policy and creates support tickets, but escalates personal exceptions.
lessons.technicalExample: Trigger phrases: book travel, travel policy; question: policy, approval status, or ticket; knowledge answer from travel site; tool branch after confirmation.

misconception.myth: Adding more trigger phrases and more tools always makes an agent conversation better.
misconception.reality: Good conversations use representative phrases, focused questions, grounded answers, confirmations for actions, and escalation when the request is sensitive or unclear.

lessons.examTakeaway: For conversation-design scenarios, reward the option that narrows intent, asks only needed questions, grounds answers in approved knowledge, confirms tool actions, and escalates risky cases.
lessons.recap: Create better agent conversations by combining clear instructions, realistic trigger phrases, focused questions, grounded answers, confirmations, tools, and escalation paths.
lessons.simplerExplanation: A grounded agent is like a careful travel concierge: it checks the official guidebook, asks for the destination only when needed, books only after confirmation, and calls a specialist for exceptions.
lessons.anotherExample: Alpine Ski House designs a gear-rental agent that answers sizing questions from approved guidance, asks dates before checking inventory, confirms before creating a reservation, and escalates injury-related questions.

lessons.title: Manage, publish, monitor, and govern agents
lessons.summary: Manage Copilot Studio agents through testing, publishing, channels, authentication, analytics, evaluations, environments, solutions, Agent 365 visibility, and governance policies.
learningObjectives: Describe how testing and publishing prepare an agent for users
Identify channels, authentication, and environments used to expose agents
Explain how analytics and evaluations monitor agent quality
Choose governance controls for agent visibility and lifecycle management
lessons.explanation:
An agent is not finished when the first conversation works. Like a storefront, it needs a front door, access rules, monitoring, and a safe way to make changes. For Copilot Studio agents, management includes testing, publishing to channels, authentication, analytics, evaluations, lifecycle packaging, and governance.

Before publishing, test the agent with realistic prompts, expected wrong turns, and sensitive requests. Publishing makes the agent available through **channels** such as Teams, websites, Microsoft Copilot experiences, or other supported endpoints. Authentication controls whether users must sign in and whether the agent can access restricted resources.

After release, use analytics and monitoring to understand usage, performance, topic behavior, and user outcomes. Agent evaluations add repeatable tests that check quality and safety before and after changes. Current PL-900 skills also mention **Microsoft Agent 365**, which provides registry visibility and observability for Copilot Studio agents in a tenant.

For lifecycle, keep agents in appropriate environments and package components with solutions when moving between development, test, and production. Governance includes Power Platform data policies, connector controls, ownership, and review.

terminology.definition: A place where users can access a published agent.
A sign-in configuration that controls identity and access.
Repeatable testing that measures quality and behavior.
A Power Platform package for lifecycle management.
A governance rule that controls connector use and data movement risk.

lessons.businessScenario: Contoso HR wants HR Helper in Teams for employees only, with analytics, evaluations, solution-based releases, and tenant visibility.
lessons.technicalExample: Checklist: test paths, require Microsoft authentication, publish to Teams, monitor adoption, run evaluations, move components through environments with solutions, and apply connector data policies.

misconception.myth: Publishing an agent to Teams means it is fully governed for the rest of its life.
misconception.reality: Publishing is only one step; owners still manage authentication, channel access, analytics, evaluations, environments, solutions, policies, and ownership.

lessons.examTakeaway: Management questions often ask what happens after build: channels decide where users access the agent, authentication decides who signs in, analytics and evaluations measure behavior, and solutions/environments support lifecycle.
lessons.recap: Manage Copilot Studio agents through testing, publishing, channels, authentication, analytics, evaluations, environments, solutions, Agent 365 visibility, and governance policies.
lessons.simplerExplanation: Managing an agent is like running a staffed kiosk in a company lobby: you choose where it stands, check employee badges, review service logs, test new scripts, and move updates through a back office before changing the live kiosk.
lessons.anotherExample: Woodgrove Bank pilots a benefits agent in a test environment, packages it in a solution, publishes it to Teams with Microsoft authentication, monitors unresolved sessions, and uses evaluations before each update.
